questions.stem: How does ServiceNow help companies manage third parties without emails and spreadsheets?
questions.explanation: The Third-party Portal is ServiceNow's solution for managing third-party communications without emails and spreadsheets. It consolidates assessments, document requests, issues, and contacts into a single system. Options A and C describe internal components, not the external-facing portal that replaces email/spreadsheet workflows.

questions.stem: What is the definition of 'Risk Management'?

options.text: Process to identify, assess, and respond to risks, threats and vulnerabilities that could compromise the business
The process of conforming to standards, policies, and remediation of audit findings
The elimination of vulnerable surface area in an enterprise environment
Policies/Standards/Procedures established to ensure an organization is aligned with corporate strategy and expectations are clearly defined

questions.explanation: Risk Management is defined as the process to identify, assess, and respond to risks, threats, and vulnerabilities that could compromise the business. Option B describes Compliance, option C describes Vulnerability Management, and option D describes Governance (establishing policies/standards/procedures).

questions.stem: What application provides the ability to define multiple levels of approvals based on business rule definitions?
questions.explanation: The Approval Configurator (GRC Approval Configurator) enables defining multiple levels of approvals based on business rule definitions. It is enabled via Policy and Compliance properties and provides granular, multi-level approval flows for GRC processes including TPRM.

questions.stem: Which table stores the third-party records?
questions.explanation: In TPRM, third-party records are stored in the Vendor [sn_vdr_vendor] table. This is distinct from Company [core_company] which stores general company records. The sn_vdr_vendor table is specifically designed for third-party risk management with fields for tier, risk rating, and assessment-related data.

questions.stem: When the GRC: Policy and Compliance Management application is installed, what GRC related list displays on the Third-party Risk Issue record?
questions.explanation: When GRC Policy and Compliance Management is installed alongside TPRM, the Citations related list appears on the Third-party Risk Issue record. Citations link risk issues to specific policy/compliance requirements, enabling traceability between third-party risk findings and organizational compliance obligations.

questions.stem: What is the advantage of using both TPRM and GRC/IRM?

options.text: Non-compliant controls automatically adjust the risk score for a third-party entity
Primary third-party contacts can then see their overall non-compliant risk score
All compliance controls are automatically visible to the third-party risk manager
Third-party Risk engagements automatically match with Audit engagements

questions.explanation: When TPRM is integrated with GRC/IRM, non-compliant controls automatically adjust the risk score for a third-party entity. This integration enables control compliance status to directly feed into vendor risk scoring, providing a holistic view of third-party risk that combines assessment results with compliance posture.

questions.stem: As a final step before closing the Third-party Risk Assessment, what task(s) would the Risk Assessor typically do?

options.text: Review comments and evaluates the risk

questions.explanation: Before closing a Third-party Risk Assessment, the Risk Assessor reviews comments and evaluates the risk. This is the final review step where the assessor confirms the overall risk picture. Flagging questions (A) and creating issues (C) happen earlier during the Generating Observations phase, and tiering (D) is a separate pre-assessment process.

questions.stem: How are Third-party Risk questionnaires and document requests displayed on the Third-party Portal?

options.text: As separate requests and can be assigned to different third-party contacts
As a single assessment assigned to a single engagement contact
As separate requests and can only be assigned to the same third-party contact
As a single assessment assigned to a single third-party contact

questions.explanation: Questionnaires and document requests are displayed as separate requests on the Third-party Portal and can be assigned to different third-party contacts. This allows the primary contact to delegate specific questionnaires to subject matter experts within their organization (e.g., IT security questions to the CISO, financial questions to the CFO).

questions.stem: What other record is created when an element classification is created?
questions.explanation: When an element classification is created, an Engagement component definition is also created. Element classifications (Service, Product, Facility) define the type of goods/services a third party provides. The corresponding engagement component definition links this classification to specific engagements for assessment purposes.

questions.stem: To what do third parties have direct access?

options.text: Update and respond to issues and tasks
View other third party’s assessment responses
View other third party’s issues and tasks

questions.explanation: Third parties have direct access to update and respond to issues and tasks through the Third-party Portal. They cannot view other third parties' assessments (B), modify issue remediation workflows (C), or view other third parties' issues (D). The portal is scoped so each third party only sees their own data.

questions.stem: What are benefits of creating Question Banks? (Choose two.)

options.text: An entire category and all its metrics from a question bank can be added to a questionnaire template
The auto assessment generator can randomly select metrics from a question bank to create a questionnaire template
Responses to individual metrics belonging to a question bank will be tracked in the question bank
Individual metrics from a question bank can be added to a questionnaire template

questions.explanation: Question Banks allow: (A) an entire category and all its metrics to be added to a questionnaire template, and (D) individual metrics from a question bank to be added to a questionnaire template. The auto-assessment generator does not randomly select from banks (B), and responses are tracked at the assessment level, not in the question bank itself (C).

questions.stem: What statements can be made about the Third-party tier? (Choose two.)

options.text: It is leveraged to decide whether to do business with a third-party, or not
It is leveraged to identify the appropriate assessment to send to the third-party
It is required to generate a third-party assessment
It can be manually set or set via the Third-party Tiering process

questions.explanation: The third-party tier: (B) is leveraged to identify the appropriate assessment to send to the third-party — higher-risk tiers get more comprehensive assessments; and (D) can be manually set or set via the Third-party Tiering process (automated scoring from tiering questionnaire). It is not required to generate assessments (C), and tier determines assessment scope, not whether to do business at all (A).

questions.stem: What application provides the capability to define multiple levels of approvals for an employee with the sn_grc_appr.admin role?
questions.explanation: The Approval Configurator provides the capability to define multiple levels of approvals. It is part of the GRC framework and can be used by employees with the sn_grc_appr.admin role. The other options (Multiple Approver Manager, Multi-level Approval Manager, IRQ ApprovalConfigurator) are not real ServiceNow application names.

questions.stem: What can be said concerning the number of third-party contacts?

options.text: A third party must have one designated internal third-party manager
A third party can designate more than one contact as the primary, but must have a minimum of one primary contact
A third party can only designate one contact as the primary contact, but may have multiple non-primary contacts
A third party can only designate one contact as the primary and must have a minimum of one non-primary contact

questions.explanation: A third party can only designate one contact as the primary contact, but may have multiple non-primary contacts. The primary contact receives assessments, can delegate work, and manages other contacts. Non-primary contacts handle assigned questionnaires and tasks. Having exactly one primary contact ensures clear accountability.

questions.stem: What are benefits of using the Third-party Portal? (Choose two.)

options.text: The Third-party Portal consolidates all communications and artifacts to a single system of truth
Third-party Portal allows the Third-party Risk Assessor team to reassign parts of a Inherent Risk Assessment
The Third-party Portal matches a database of documents to document requests
The Third-party Portal reduces risk for an organization by enabling secure communications with the third-party
The Third-party Portal can be leveraged by the third party to work with other partners

questions.explanation: Benefits of the Third-party Portal: (A) consolidates all communications and artifacts to a single system of truth — replacing emails and spreadsheets; and (D) reduces risk by enabling secure communications with the third party. The portal does not allow reassigning Inherent Risk Assessments (B), match document databases (C), or allow third parties to collaborate with other partners (E).

questions.stem: What is the minimum role required to create event-driven rules?
questions.explanation: The minimum role required to create event-driven rules is sn_vdr_risk_asmt.vendor_risk_admin. Event-driven rules are a configuration/administration function that auto-generates and sends questionnaires and document requests. The admin role is needed because these rules affect the assessment workflow for all third parties.

questions.stem: If a Third-party Risk Issue is for internal use only, what states can be skipped? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: If a Third-party Risk Issue is for internal use only, the 'Finalize with Third-party' (B) and 'Submitted to Third-party' (D) states can be skipped. These states involve external third-party interaction, which is unnecessary for internal-only issues. The New (C) and Analyze (A) states are still required for internal processing.

questions.stem: The assessment page provides an area to import what kind of a completed questionnaire?
questions.explanation: The assessment page provides an area to import a completed SIG (Standardized Information Gathering) questionnaire. SIG is an industry-standard questionnaire format used for third-party risk assessments. ServiceNow supports importing completed SIG questionnaires from spreadsheets to streamline the assessment process.

questions.stem: To which application do you navigate to customize the Third-party Portal?
questions.explanation: The Third-party Portal is built on Service Portal, so you navigate to Service Portal to customize it. Service Portal provides the widget framework, page layouts, and theming capabilities used by the Third-party Portal (/svdp). Now Experience Framework (C) is for workspace UIs, not portal customization.

questions.stem: How are Assessment Templates [sn_vdr_risk_asmt_template] related to Questionnaire Templates [asmt_metric_type]?

options.text: By a reference field on Questionnaire Template [asmt_metric_type] (One-to-many)
By a reference field on Assessment Template [sn_vdr_risk_asmt_template] (Many-to-one)

questions.explanation: Assessment Templates and Questionnaire Templates are related through the M2M (many-to-many) table sn_vdr_risk_asmt_m2m_asmt_template_questionnaire_template. This allows one assessment template to include multiple questionnaire templates, and one questionnaire template to be used across multiple assessment templates.

questions.stem: A Third-party Risk Manager needs to run a report displaying Third-party Assessments due. On which table would this report be run?
questions.explanation: To run a report displaying Third-party Assessments due, the report should be run on the sn_vdr_risk_asmt_assessment table. This is the main assessment table that tracks assessment records including due dates, states, and third-party associations. The task table (B) is for individual tasks, and the issue table (D) is for risk issues.

questions.stem: As a primary contact, a new third-party contact can be added via 'Manage Team' and then selecting what?
questions.explanation: As a primary contact in the Third-party Portal, a new third-party contact can be added via 'Manage Team' and then selecting 'Invite Contact.' This sends an invitation to the new contact with login credentials. The primary contact has the ability to manage team members including creating new contacts.

questions.stem: What functions can be performed in the Third-party Portal? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Third-party Portal enables: (A) managing assessment deadlines — contacts can track and manage due dates for their assessments; and (B) completing assessments — the primary function of the portal. General project management (C) and hosting web meetings (D) are not portal functions.

questions.stem: When will the tiering value be updated on the third-party record?

options.text: When the inherent risk assessment record state is Responses Received
When all inherent risk assessments have been completed
When the inherent risk assessment record state is closed
When all inherent risk assessments have been sent

questions.explanation: The tiering value is updated on the third-party record when the inherent risk assessment record state is closed. The tiering score is calculated from assessment responses, mapped to risk tiers (None/Low/Minor/Moderate/High/Critical), and then assigned to the third party upon assessment closure.

questions.stem: What does accepting an Issue mark?

options.text: An implication that the known control failure is unimportant
An intention to create an exception for a known control failure or risk
Special third parties get an exception

questions.explanation: Accepting an Issue marks an intention to create an exception for a known control failure or risk. It acknowledges the risk exists but accepts it rather than remediating it. This is different from ignoring the failure (A), indicating failed remediation (C), or creating special vendor exceptions (D).

questions.stem: What is the relationship between records in the third-party element table and records in the third-party element classification table?

options.text: For each element, there can be many classifications.
The ratio relationship can vary. An element could have no classification, one classification, or many classifications.
For each classification, there can be only one element.
Many elements could have the same classification

questions.explanation: Many elements can have the same classification. Element classifications (Service, Product, Facility) are categories that apply broadly — for example, multiple third-party elements could all be classified as 'Service.' The relationship is many-to-one: many elements share one classification, but each element has one classification.

questions.stem: What methods in the baseline can be used to assign a Third-party Risk Assessment to a third party? (Choose three.)

options.text: Automated based on Security Score rule
Automated based on Third-party Tier rule
Automated based on Business Services supported by the third party

questions.explanation: Baseline methods to assign a Third-party Risk Assessment: (A) Manual — TPR manager manually creates and assigns; (B) Automated based on third-party categorization — rules triggered by category; (D) Automated based on third-party tier rule — tier determines assessment type. Security Score rules (C) and Business Services (E) are not baseline assignment methods.

questions.stem: What statement best describes what happens when a question in a Third-party Risk Assessment is related to a Control Objective?

options.text: Control Objectives with the Vendor Entity are automatically assigned a Question from a Questionnaire Assessment
The Control Objective is updated as the third party completes the questionnaire
Associated Controls are marked automatically as Non-Compliant or Compliant based on the response of the third party
A Question can only be related to one Control Objective at a time

questions.explanation: When a question in a Third-party Risk Assessment is related to a Control Objective, associated Controls are marked automatically as Non-Compliant or Compliant based on the third party's response. This integration between TPRM assessments and GRC controls enables automated compliance tracking from assessment answers.

questions.stem: To what type of assessment record can a third-party contact respond?
questions.explanation: Third-party contacts can respond to third-party risk assessments through the Third-party Portal. Tiering assessments (A) are completed by internal stakeholders, not external contacts. IRQ assessments (C) are internal risk questionnaires. Risk Area assessments (D) are not a standard TPRM assessment type.

questions.stem: What are the application scopes to be considered when making changes to the Vendor Management Workspace? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: When making changes to the Vendor Management Workspace, consider: (C) GRC: Third-party Risk Management Workspace (sn_tprm_ws) — the new TPRM workspace scope; and (D) GRC: Vendor Risk Management Workspace (sn_vrm_ws) — the legacy VRM scope. Both scopes contain UI components used in the workspace. ITSM vendor components (A) and Common Core (B) are separate.

questions.stem: In addition to direct third-party assessments, what other hierarchical entities can contribute to the overall third-party risk rating? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: In addition to direct third-party assessments, (B) Engagements and (C) Child third parties contribute to the overall third-party risk rating. Engagements are assessed separately and their scores roll up. Child third parties (subsidiaries) have their own assessments that aggregate to the parent. Advanced risk assessments (A) and entity class rules (D) are not hierarchical contributors.

questions.stem: If clean data is not provided by the customer, what baseline solutions are available within the platform? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Baseline data cleansing solutions within the platform: (A) System import transform map scripts — transform data during import; (B) System definition fix scripts module — one-time scripted cleanup; (E) Field normalization plugin — declarative rules to normalize field values. Integration Hub ETL (C) is an add-on, and Service Graph Connector (D) is CMDB-specific, not general data cleansing.

questions.stem: What can be created with the Template Designer? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The Template Designer can create: (C) Document Request Templates and (D) Questionnaire Templates. The Template Designer is specifically designed for building these two types of assessment components with a visual canvas, question controls, categories, and scoring options. Assessment Templates (B) and Risk Assessments (A) are created elsewhere.

questions.stem: What are the features of Third-party Risk Issues? (Choose two.)

options.text: Generate audit tasks for the third-party risk team
Provide third parties direct access to update and respond to Issues
Can be generated on-demand or automatically due to an incorrect answer
Can only be seen by the customer's risk team

questions.explanation: Features of Third-party Risk Issues: (B) provide third parties direct access to update and respond to issues through the portal; and (C) can be generated on-demand or automatically due to an incorrect answer on an assessment. Issues are visible in the portal (not hidden from third parties), and they don't generate audit tasks (A).

questions.stem: What do third-party risk event-driven rules do?

options.text: Auto-generate issue records when third parties are not compliant
Auto-generate and send questionnaires and document requests to engagements and third parties
Auto-generate engagements when risk intelligence scores fall below specified levels
Auto-generate and send email notifications to third parties for engagements

questions.explanation: Event-driven rules auto-generate and send questionnaires and document requests to engagements and third parties. This is confirmed by the ServiceNow docs: 'When an event-driven management rule runs, it auto-generates and sends questionnaires and doc requests to third parties.' They do not auto-generate issues (A), engagements (C), or email notifications (D).

questions.stem: What are the benefits of performing a Third-party Risk Assessment? (Choose two.)

options.text: To have a stronger negotiating position for future contracts
To have third parties demonstrate that they operate their business at an acceptable risk level to your organization
To understand with whom you are working when you partner with third parties
To put the ownership on the third party to prove that they manage risk at a level with which the third party is comfortable

questions.explanation: Benefits of performing a Third-party Risk Assessment: (B) have third parties demonstrate they operate at an acceptable risk level to your organization; and (C) understand with whom you are working when partnering with third parties. Option A (negotiating position) is procurement, not risk assessment. Option D puts ownership on the third party for their own comfort level, not yours.

questions.stem: What are the element classification values in the ServiceNow baseline for Third-party Risk Management? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The baseline element classification values in ServiceNow TPRM are: (A) Service, (C) Product, and (E) Facility. These three classifications categorize the types of goods, services, or support that third parties provide. Principal (B) and Manufacturer (D) are not baseline element classification values in TPRM.

questions.stem: What type of record is each question in an assessment?
questions.explanation: Each question in an assessment is an Assessment Metric [asmt_metric] record. The Template Designer docs confirm this terminology: 'Metric' = a single question within a questionnaire template. Metrics belong to Categories (groups of related questions) within a Metric Type (questionnaire template).

questions.stem: What purpose do ServiceNow third-party risk engagements serve?

options.text: They give a third-party risk manager a way of scheduling workshops with the customer to help the third party become compliant
They give a way for a third-party risk manager to assess risks and measure third-party CSAT performance
They give a third-party risk manager a way to assess risks at the products or services level
They give a third-party risk manager a way to assess the validity of the third-party assessment responses

questions.explanation: Engagements give a third-party risk manager a way to assess risks at the products or services level. An engagement represents the relationship with a third party for specific goods, services, or support. This granularity allows different risk assessments for different services provided by the same third party.

questions.stem: What are ways that the third-party records can be created? (Choose three.)

options.text: Through integration with an existing supplier management system
By manual data entry or through a due diligence onboarding request

questions.explanation: Third-party records can be created: (B) through integration with an existing supplier management system; (D) by manual data entry or through a due diligence onboarding request; and (E) by importing data (spreadsheet import). The Third-party Portal (A) is for external contacts, not for creating third-party records. Operator records (C) do not convert to third-party records.

questions.stem: What are the functions of the Third-party Risk Assessor? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create issues for the third party
Access completed assessments from third parties
Create a Primary Contact record for a third party

questions.explanation: Functions of the Third-party Risk Assessor: (B) create issues for the third party during assessment review; (D) access completed assessments from third parties; and (E) create a Primary Contact record for a third party. Updating contract deadlines (A) is not an assessor function, and enabling cross-vendor communications (C) is not possible.

questions.stem: When should the third-party risk assessor create Issues based on the third-party assessment response?

options.text: Any time, as long as at least one question has been answered
When the assessment is in theSubmitted to Third-party state
When the assessment is in the "Generating Observations" state
When the assessment is in the "Finalizing with Third-party" state

questions.explanation: The third-party risk assessor creates Issues when the assessment is in the 'Finalizing with Third-party' state. At this point, the assessor has reviewed the third party's responses and identified gaps or concerns. Issues are created after response review but before final closure. 'Generating Observations' (C) is an earlier state.

questions.stem: A requirement of this customer’s implementation is to be able to track third-party subsidiaries separately from the third party but to roll up the scoring to the (primary) third party. What action do you take to fulfill this requirement?

options.text: In the Related Links of the (primary) third party record, click Add Child third party and add each subsidiary
Populate the Children field on the (primary) third party record with all of the subsidiaries
From the Navigation, select Third party Risk, select Third party, then select All Child Third parties; Select New to create a new child third party record for each subsidiary
On the Child third party related list of the (primary) third party, click the New button and add a third party record for each subsidiary
In addition to the (primary) third party record, create a third party record for each subsidiary and fill the Parent field with the name of the (primary) third party

questions.explanation: To track subsidiaries separately while rolling up scoring to the parent third party, create a third-party record for each subsidiary and populate the Parent field with the primary third party's name. This establishes the parent-child hierarchy enabling score rollup while maintaining separate assessment tracking for each subsidiary.

questions.stem: What Vendor Management workspace feature gives a rendering of the geographical locations of active third parties and engagements?
questions.explanation: The Risk concentration map in the Vendor Management Workspace gives a rendering of geographical locations of active third parties and engagements. It uses Google Maps and can be filtered by risk ratings and engagement types. Access via Workspaces > Vendor Management Workspace > Risk tab > map icon.

questions.stem: What types of requests can be made by an employee selecting the Request third-party risk due diligence option? (Choose four.)

options.text: Offboard an engagement with due diligence
Reassess an existing engagement for contract renewal

questions.explanation: The due diligence request options are: Onboard a new engagement (F), Reassess an existing engagement (E), Reassess for contract renewal (D), Offboard with due diligence (C), and Offboard without due diligence. Since the question asks for 4 of these, and Duplicate (A) and Cancel (B) are not valid options, the answer is C, D, E, F.

questions.stem: What can primary third-party contacts do in the Third-party Portal? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Primary third-party contacts in the portal can: (B) respond to issues from the assessing organization; (C) manage third-party contacts (add/remove team members, delegate work); and (E) respond to assessments. They cannot manage assessment templates (A) — that's an admin function — or customize the portal itself (D).

questions.stem: Which related list is used when relating a Third party assessment question to a Control Objective record?
questions.explanation: The Assessment Metrics related list is used when relating a Third-party assessment question to a Control Objective record. Since each question is an Assessment Metric [asmt_metric], the relationship between questions and Control Objectives is managed through the assessment metrics related list on the Control Objective form.

questions.stem: Elements can be defined on an engagement. What do these elements represent?

options.text: An external organization on which the third party relies to provide goods, services, or support
Component criteria for the engagement applicable to the third party's delivery of goods, services, or support.
Risk areas defined for the engagement applicable to the third party's delivery of goods, services, or support.
The goods, services, or support that is provided by the third party

questions.explanation: Elements defined on an engagement represent the goods, services, or support that is provided by the third party. Each element can be classified (Service, Product, Facility) and assessed individually within the engagement. This enables granular risk assessment at the service/product level rather than only at the overall third-party level.

questions.stem: What is the default value appended to the instance URL to access the scoped Third-party Portal according to the sn_vdr_risk_asmt.vendor_portal_endpoint system property?
questions.explanation: The default value appended to the instance URL to access the Third-party Portal is /svdp, controlled by the sn_vdr_risk_asmt.vendor_portal_endpoint system property. SVDP stands for Scoped Vendor Portal. The full URL would be https://instance.service-now.com/svdp.

questions.stem: All Assessment Metrics within a Metric Category are scored, are rolled up, and get what score range?
questions.explanation: Assessment Metrics within a Metric Category are scored on a 0-100 scale. Individual metric scores are calculated based on responses (binary 0/100 when Scored checkbox is on, or normalized from scale definitions) and then rolled up to category and overall assessment scores, all within the 0-100 range.

questions.stem: What create actions can be triggered from the Rule Actions tab of a Provider-Based Submission Rule? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Provider-Based Submission Rules can trigger: (A) Create assessment — generate an assessment for the third party; (C) Create third party — create a new third-party record; (D) Create primary contact — create a contact record for the third party. These are the create actions available in the Rule Actions tab that automate record creation from provider data submissions.

questions.stem: Third-party contacts are stored in the vm_vdr_contact table, which extends from which table?
questions.explanation: Third-party contacts stored in the vm_vdr_contact table extend from sys_user. This means contacts inherit all standard user fields (name, email, phone) and can authenticate to the portal. The extension adds vendor-specific fields like vendor reference and primary contact designation.

questions.stem: What actions could have an impact on the third party's Risk Assessment rating? (Choose three.)

options.text: Answering one or more questions incorrectly
Reassigning a questionnaire to a contact

questions.explanation: Actions impacting the third party's Risk Assessment rating: (A) answering questions incorrectly — wrong answers lower scores; (B) leaving answers blank — unanswered questions affect the overall rating; (C) omitting documentation — missing required documents impacts assessment completeness. Spelling errors (D) and reassigning questionnaires (E) do not affect scoring.

questions.stem: To display your company name in the portal, change which ServiceNow property?
questions.explanation: To display your company name in the Third-party Portal, change the sn_vdr_risk_asmt.company.name system property. This property controls the organization name shown to third-party contacts when they access the portal. The other options have incorrect property name formats.

questions.stem: What actions must be taken before a risk intelligence report can be requested? (Choose two.)

options.text: A risk intelligence sample report must be downloaded by the user
The Order reports field of the provider record must be set to true
The Sanctioned report request field of the provider record must be set to yes
A risk intelligence request type record must be created for the provider
The copyright agreement field on the Risk Intelligence Report request form must be set to true.

questions.explanation: Before requesting a risk intelligence report: (B) the Order reports field of the provider record must be set to true — enabling report ordering for that provider; and (D) a risk intelligence request type record must be created for the provider — defining what type of reports can be requested. These two configurations are required before reports can be ordered.

questions.stem: Who are able to change the password for the third-party contact? (Choose two.)

options.text: Third-party contact via the Forgot Password link

questions.explanation: Passwords for third-party contacts can be changed by: (B) the third-party contact themselves via the Forgot Password link on the portal login page; and (C) a sys_admin who has full user management capabilities. Contract Relationship Managers (A) and Risk Reviewers (D) do not have password management privileges.

questions.stem: What will be available to Supplier Lifecycle Operations (SLO) from Third-party Risk Management (TPRM) once suppliers respond to assessments if during onboarding, SLO requests due diligence on a supplier from TPRM?
questions.explanation: When Supplier Lifecycle Operations (SLO) requests due diligence from TPRM and suppliers respond to assessments, the final risk scores become available to SLO. This integration enables procurement decisions to incorporate risk assessment results from TPRM, ensuring informed supplier management based on risk evaluation outcomes.

questions.stem: In which table are Third-party Risk Tasks stored?
questions.explanation: Third-party Risk Tasks are stored in the sn_vdr_risk_asmt_task table. This follows the TPRM naming convention where sn_vdr_risk_asmt is the application scope prefix. The task table extends the base task table and includes fields specific to third-party risk management workflows.

questions.stem: By default, when are reminder notifications for pending assessments sent to the third party contact? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: By default, reminder notifications for pending assessments are sent to the third-party contact at 3 days prior (C) and 7 days prior (D) to the due date. These baseline notification intervals give contacts reasonable advance warning to complete their assessments on time. Options A and B (14 days after and 30 days prior) are not default intervals.

questions.stem: When should a Third-party Risk Issue be created? (Choose three.)

options.text: When identifying a risk to a business
When the third party does not include documentation required as part of an assessment
When a response to a question in the risk assessment is not satisfactory
When there is more than one third-party contact submitting responses
When there are items that require additional follow-up

questions.explanation: Third-party Risk Issues should be created when: (B) the third party does not include required documentation; (C) a response to a question is not satisfactory; and (E) there are items requiring additional follow-up. Issues are not created simply for identifying business risks (A) or because multiple contacts submit responses (D).
